title: Detection of Small-Molecule Aggregation with High-Throughput Microplate Biophysical Methods
protocol: Turn on the RWG instrument 60 minutes prior to use.
Dispense 30 µl of filtered buffer into each well of a 384-well assay plate.
Centrifuge the plate for 3 min at 336 × g, 20°C.
Incubate the plate at room temperature for 120 min.
Read the buffer baseline.
Add 30 μl DMSO to columns 2-11 and 14-23 of a 384-well source plate.
Add 60 μl of 10 mM stock compound to columns 1 and 13 and mix.
Transfer 30 μl from column 1 to column 2.
Repeat the transfer to the next column across the plate to column 11 to obtain an eleven-point, two-fold serial dilution of the compound.
Repeat for columns 13-23.
Place 30 μl DMSO in each well of columns 12 and 24 as negative controls.
Centrifuge compound source plate for 5 min at 2103 × g, 20°C.
Dispense 300 nl from the source plate to the 384-well assay plate replicating the layout.
Centrifuge plate for 3 min at 336 × g, 20°C.
Incubate plate for 60 min at 20°C in the RWG instrument.
Read plate using the same settings as previously specified.
Inspect the data for linear changes in wavelength shift below and above the critical aggregation concentration (CAC).
Fit the data below the CAC to a straight line using the equation y1 = m1x + c1.
Fit the data above the CAC to a second straight line using the equation y2 = m2x + c2.
Calculate the CAC as the concentration at which the two lines intersect, using the formula (c2 − c1)/(m1 − m2).
Identify any “hook effect” where the response increases with concentration and then decreases due to large aggregates or compound precipitation.
Truncate the analysis concentration range prior to the hook if a decrease is observed.
Calculate the mean response plus six times the standard deviation for control wells containing buffer and 1% (v/v) DMSO.
Use this calculated threshold to determine if compounds are aggregating at one or more concentrations.
Consider a compound as aggregating if its response is greater than the threshold at any concentration tested.
Estimate the CAC for an aggregating compound as the lowest tested concentration where the threshold is crossed.
Inspect data to ensure six times standard deviation cutoff is reasonable, especially in cases with large standard deviations.
For data with high variability, use the average response plus three times the standard deviation as a more appropriate threshold.
Turn on DLS instrument at least 30 min prior to use and set temperature to 25°C.
Clean bench with ethanol to remove dust particles.
Place plate cover supplied with the assay plates on the bottom of a 384-well plate.
Illuminate the plate with a flashlight in a fume hood and tilt plate to spot large dust particles.
Remove any dust particles with 10-s bursts of N2.
Cover plate or place inside a plastic bag after cleaning to avoid contamination.
Centrifuge compound stock solutions for 10 min at 14,000 × g (e.g., 12,000 rpm in a F45-24-11 rotor), 20°C.
Dispense 30 µl of assay buffer into specified wells.
Use a multichannel pipette to add 30 μl of DMSO to columns 2-11 and 14-23 of a 384-well source plate.
Add 60 μl of 10 mM stock compound to columns 1 and 13, then mix thoroughly.
Transfer 30 μl from column 1 to column 2.
Repeat the transfer process sequentially across the plate to column 11 to create an eleven-point, two-fold serial dilution of the compound.
Perform the same procedure for columns 13-23.
Place 30 μl of DMSO in each well of columns 12 and 24 as negative controls.
Add 30 μl of a positive control such as miconazole nitrate to at least one eleven-point two-fold dilution point.
Centrifuge the plate for 5 min at 583 × g (e.g., 1500 rpm in a TX-1000 rotor) at 20°C to remove bubbles.
Centrifuge compound source plate for 5 min at 2103 × g (e.g., 3000 rpm in a TX-1000 rotor), 20°C.
Dispense 300 nl of test substance from the source plate into specified wells of the 384-well assay plate.
Add 30 μl of buffer to each well, achieving a final DMSO concentration of 1% (v/v).
Centrifuge plate for 3 min at 583 × g (e.g., 1500 rpm in a TX-1000 rotor), 20°C.
Visually check the plates for bubbles after centrifugation.
Spray the bottom of the assay plate with 10-s bursts of nitrogen to remove particles if necessary.
Place assay plate in DLS instrument for at least 15 min to allow equilibration to 25°C.
Layer 5 µl silicon or paraffin oil on each well if experiments exceed 1.5 hr.
Reduce buffer volume to 25 µl when using oil.
Add 25 nl compound or DMSO after reducing buffer volume.
Add 5 µl oil before final centrifugation if used.
Ensure oil does not touch the bottom of the plate.
Collect DLS data with parameters set for DynaPro Plate Reader II.
Set number of times to measure each well to 1.
Enable Auto-attenuation and acquire an image of each well.
Set number of DLS acquisitions to 10.
Set temperature to 25°C.
Set DLS acquisition time between 3 to 5 seconds.
Increase DLS acquisition time for large particles if necessary.
Open data in DLS software after removing the plate.
Set cutoffs for data analysis between 1.5 µs and 1 s.
Add a data filter in summary table to mask acquisitions with an autocorrelation intensity outside of baseline limit of 1 ± 0.02.
Mask acquisitions with no measured particles.
Set the hydrodynamic radius of buffer control wells to zero.
Inspect the acquisitions for DMSO/buffer and buffer-only control wells.
Calculate the percentage of acquisitions with no measured particles.
Check that the autocorrelation function centers on a value of 1 and exhibits noise around the baseline.
Repeat the experiment if ≥30% of buffer/DMSO or buffer acquisitions contain particles, ensuring proper filtration of both buffer and sample to remove dust or other contaminants.
Inspect all compound acquisitions (autocorrelation plots and images) well by well.
Accept data showing an exponential decay to a value of 1 for use in calculating the hydrodynamic radius (Rh).
Exclude data from calculation if the autocorrelation function does not match the example behavior shown in Figure 5B.
Verify the regularization fit for each acquisition to confirm goodness of fit.
Set the hydrodynamic radius of the well to zero if >70% of acquisitions are particle-free.
Exclude wells from analysis if ≥30% of acquisitions are masked due to very large particles.
Exclude wells from analysis if there is large variability between acquisitions for a well.
Determine the lowest compound concentration at which particles are observed in at least 70% of acquisitions as the Lowest Aggregation Concentration (LAC).
Alternatively, analyze Rh values with linear regression to calculate the CAC if data quality is sufficient.
